title: Effect size and practical importance
outcome: Explain effect size and practical importance using the records and boundaries of this fictional investigation.
scenario: An improvement with a practical threshold. A team compares error rates against a predeclared practical threshold.
given: A makes 20 errors in 1000 tasks; B makes 15. Practical improvement requires at least 10 fewer errors per 1000.

steps.label: Compute effect size
steps.detail: B has 5 fewer errors per 1000, a 0.5-percentage-point reduction.

steps.label: Apply practical threshold
steps.detail: Five is less than ten, so the observed change misses this threshold.

explanation: Effect size describes how much the outcome changes. Practical importance depends on the real decision criterion; relative changes can sound large while absolute changes remain small.

counterfactual.prediction: The reduction becomes 12 per 1000 and meets the stated practical threshold.
counterfactual.reason: Twenty minus eight exceeds the required ten fewer errors.

student_task: Calculate the absolute error-rate reduction from 20/1000 to 15/1000. Does it meet the ten-fewer-errors threshold, and what changes when B has eight errors?
teacher_answer: A is 2%; B is 1.5%. B has 5 fewer errors per 1000, a 0.5-percentage-point reduction. Five is less than ten, so the observed change misses this threshold. Changed case: The reduction becomes 12 per 1000 and meets the stated practical threshold. Twenty minus eight exceeds the required ten fewer errors.
project_evidence: For the Reproducible AI Research Study, retain an annotated worked trace and the changed-case reasoning. Connect the claim to its records, units and assumptions so another investigator can challenge or reproduce it.
limits: No uncertainty or statistical significance is supplied; these counts alone cannot establish a general effect.
review_note: Individually authored fictional practice distinct from the reserved independent case. No invented significance, real experiment execution or pupil outcome is asserted.
